Yes. instant, hafley-rs and hafley-rxjs are all on main and level with origin. I checked this turn.

Not on main, by design:
- The wave-3 cutover stays on branch `refactor/lift-wave-3`.
- Uncommitted files from other sessions stay local: the instant `artifacts/*.png`, the `issues/*` directories and the hafley-rxjs bewpp edits.
- The wave-3 cutover stays on branch refactor/lift-wave-3. whats this mean?

The wave-3 cutover moved instant's terminal/TUI code out of instant and into the `@hafley66/boop-xterm` package.

1. It was merged into instant main.
2. The driver broke: the squares piled up at the top, and turn debug froze on scroll.
3. The merge was reverted on main. That is why main works now.
4. The work is not lost. It sits on branch `refactor/lift-wave-3`, worktree `~/projects/instant/.boop-worktrees/refactor/lift-wave-3`.

Nothing uses that branch now. It lands on main again only once the strip regression is found and fixed.

Yes. A fork is now working on it: **instant: wave-3 cutover re-land (fix/the-gang-relands-wave-3)**.

The fork's steps:
1. Merge main into `refactor/lift-wave-3`, keeping the cutover plus main's `Strip.window` fix.
2. Find the cause of the "squares pile at top" regression, with file:line evidence.
3. Move the strip-push turn visibility into boop-xterm, which drops its polling path.
4. Write a red test first, then the fix. Then build a boop-xterm browser test from a capture of a real session (this one, pane `s:le-blog-3`). It will write PNGs of the strip, scrolled turn debug and tool-block labels to `hafley-rxjs/packages/boop-xterm/artifacts/`.

The fork works only on branches and worktrees. It will not touch instant main or your running `just dev`, and it will not merge. You get the PNGs to check before anything lands.
